units.unmetFlightDemand: percentage points by which enplanement growth exceeds departure growth across the window
units.delay: arrival delay minutes per arrival with weather delay removed, 2024
units.growth: percent change in enplanements across the window

sources.name: FAA ACAIS calendar-year enplanements at commercial service airports
sources.vintage: CY2024 final, with the CY2023 comparative column

sources.name: FAA slot administration Level 2 and Level 3 airports

gaps: No free source publishes gate or terminal capacity, so congestion uses enplanements per open runway; FAA ASPM declared rates are login-gated.
Long-haul share counts BTS domestic reporting-carrier departures over 2,000 miles. International long-haul is out of scope because T-100 Segment has no stable bulk download.
Departure counts and delay minutes cover BTS reporting carriers only, so unmet flight demand omits carriers under the 1% revenue reporting threshold.
Territories have no US Census division, so their region is null and they never appear in a division ranking.
FAA CY2025 enplanements were still preliminary at ingest, so the comparison window is the latest two final calendar years.
